answer: Curvature-Toll Coordination Market: each epoch an agent publishes a quill—a random-walk fingerprint over its recent counterparties. The protocol computes local graph curvature and charges every coordinated action a toll proportional to curvature² and the spectral gap; tolls peak at the epoch’s zenith. Sybils that forge dense mutual interactions create high-curvature cliques, so N coordinated identities incur superlinear tolls (roughly O(N²)), making mass coordination costlier than honest sparse coordination.
